Recovery Time Objective: maximum acceptable delay between service interruption and restoration.
Recovery Point Objective: maximum acceptable time since the last data recovery point (i.e., data loss window).
RPO/RTO hours; lowest cost; restore data and redeploy infrastructure with IaC in the recovery Region.
RPO/RTO tens of minutes; data replicated live, core infrastructure provisioned but app servers off until failover.
RPO seconds, RTO minutes; scaled-down but fully functional copy running; scale up on failover.
Near-zero RPO/RTO; full production in multiple Regions serving traffic; highest cost and complexity.
System keeps working without needing changes during a failure (e.g., pre-provisioned capacity in each AZ/Region).
Control plane: APIs to create/modify resources. Data plane: the running service. Rely on data planes during recovery; they are more available.
Serial hard dependencies multiply: two 99.9% components in series ≈ 99.8%.
Independent redundant components: 1 − (1 − A)^n; two 99% components in parallel ≈ 99.99%.
99.9% ≈ 8.76 hours/year; 99.99% ≈ 52.6 minutes/year; 99.999% ≈ 5.26 minutes/year.
